questions.question: You create a Content Understanding analyzer field that must return one of five fixed incident types. Which method should you use?

options.text: No method, because enumerations are not supported
options.why: Classification fields with enumerations are supported.

options.text: generate, with no enumeration
options.why: Generate lets the model write any value, so consistency is not guaranteed.

options.text: extract, with a description of the five types
options.why: Extract returns text that is written in the document, which might not match the list.

options.text: classify, with the five values as an enumeration
options.why: Correct. Classify selects from the list you supply.

questions.explanation: Classify chooses from a fixed set of values.

questions.question: A claims team wants an agent to read forms and open a claim only when values are reliable. A handwritten policy number is often unclear. What should you do?

options.text: Change every field to the generate method
options.why: Generated values are less tied to the page and are harder to verify.

options.text: Enable confidence and source estimation, and route fields below a threshold to a person
options.why: Correct. Confidence scores identify values that need human review.

options.text: Use prebuilt-layout, which returns only Markdown
options.why: Layout analysis returns no fields to validate.

options.text: Increase the number of pages analysed per request
options.why: This does not improve the reliability of unclear handwriting.

questions.explanation: Confidence and grounding support straight-through processing with human review.

questions.question: You need clean Markdown with table structure and figure descriptions from reports to ground a RAG application. You do not need custom fields. Which analyzer fits best?

options.text: The OCR skill alone
options.why: OCR returns text without structure or figure descriptions.

options.text: A custom analyzer with a generate field per paragraph
options.why: This is more work and does not preserve layout as Markdown.

options.text: prebuilt-documentSearch
options.why: Correct. It is optimised for RAG and returns Markdown, tables, figure descriptions and a summary.

options.text: prebuilt-invoice
options.why: This returns invoice fields, which are not what reports need.

questions.explanation: Use a prebuilt RAG analyzer when no custom fields are needed.

questions.question: Creating a custom analyzer fails because no model deployment is configured. Which prerequisite is missing?

options.text: A private endpoint on the storage account
options.why: Networking is unrelated to the error.

options.text: A custom domain on the Content Understanding analyzer
options.why: Analyzers are created with an id, not a domain.

options.text: A chat model and an embedding model deployed on the Foundry resource and set as defaults
options.why: Correct. Field extraction uses the resource's own model deployments.

options.text: A semantic configuration on an Azure AI Search index
options.why: Search is not involved in analyzer creation.

questions.explanation: Content Understanding relies on default model deployments in your Foundry resource.

questions.question: A custom document analyzer needs an invoice number, a total, and a two-sentence summary for adjusters. Which two field definitions are appropriate?

options.text: InvoiceNumber and Total as extract fields
options.why: Correct. Both values are written in the document.

options.text: Summary as an extract field
options.why: There is no summary text on the page to extract.

options.text: InvoiceNumber as a generate field
options.why: A value on the page should be extracted so that it stays verifiable.

options.text: Summary as a generate field
options.why: Correct. The summary is not written in the document, so the model produces it.

questions.explanation: Use extract for values on the page and generate for values the model must write.
